title: A function's meaning changes under a new caller
class: API producer and caller disagree across files
story: A changes products() in catalog.ts to list only what's in stock, and the callers it knows about (the shop page, the product list) now hide sold-out products, as A meant. B adds a product page in index.ts that looks products up with findProduct(), which goes through products(): on B's base that finds every product. Together, the page for a sold-out product is a 404. The types are unchanged, so the type-checker has nothing to say.

a.why: stop listing products that are sold out

b.why: give each product an API page

fact.sentence: Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock

resolution: catalog.ts gains catalogEntry(id), a lookup in the whole catalog, and the product page uses it; products() keeps A's meaning.
